name: City Council Special Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 20, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER called the meeting to order at 2:31 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Fernando Estrada
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  NOVEMBER 3, 2026 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2640 canceling the
  November 3, 2026 election and appointing Britt Huff and Lisa Van Ingen Pope each
  to four-year terms of office as Council Members.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2640 CANCELING THE NOVEMBER 3, 2026
  ELECTION AND APPOINTING BRITT HUFF AND LISA VAN INGEN POPE
  EACH TO FOUR-YEAR TERMS OF OFFICE AS COUNCIL MEMBERS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2640 by title.

B.  PROPOSED WILDFIRE LIABILITY REFORMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the proposed wildfire liability reforms
  and direct staff to express the City’s opposition to the Governor’s proposal by joining
  the Cal Cities Local Government Sign-On Letter.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed concern regarding the Governor’s proposed
reforms, citing potential impacts on the City’s ability to recover costs to rebuild public facilities
following a disaster and limitations on insurers’ subrogation rights. She urged the City to
oppose the proposal and join Cal Cities’ opposition letter.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 20, 2026
 COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF echoed COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA’s concerns, noting
strong support among cities throughout Los Angeles County for opposing the proposal and
stating that it would negatively impact local governments.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the City’s State Senator had publicly expressed
significant concerns regarding the proposal’s potential impacts on local cities.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO EXPRESS THE CITY’S OPPOSITION TO THE
  GOVERNOR’S PROPOSAL BY JOINING THE CAL CITIES LOCAL
  GOVERNMENT SIGN-ON LETTER.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Zerunyan

5.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 25, 2026, at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular City Council meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

  _____
Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Pam Brown Schachter, Mayor Pro Tem

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 20, 2026
